card.name: Miles after a distance number
card.fires_on: The word miles (or a nearby closing bracket or comma) right after a spelled-out distance such as two, twenty or fifty-five, in historical place descriptions. It sits just before a compass direction or place.

modes.label: Miles after number
modes.description: The word miles follows a spelled-out number in a description of where a place lies or how far someone traveled.
modes.example: towed his primitive craft fifty-five<< miles>> by river to his home in the wilderness

modes.label: End of distance phrase
modes.description: A bracket or comma closes a distance phrase just before a direction like northwest or southwest.
modes.example: The town is 30 miles (48 km<<)>> northwest of Downtown San Antonio.

modes.label: Other quantity words
modes.description: Words like years or further follow a spelled-out amount or degree.
modes.example: It was nearly twenty<< years>> after the Osages had bought the land
